items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Pick the odd one out and give reasons: (i) Jowar, Bajra, Ragi, Chana (ii) Kidney beans, Green gram, Soya bean, Rice
items.answer: (i) Odd one out : Chana Reason : Jowar, Bajra, and Ragi are types of millets (cereals), which are primarily sources of carbohydrates. Chana (chickpea) is a pulse (legume), which is a rich source of protein. (ii) Odd one out : Rice Reason : Kidney beans (Rajma), Green gram (Moong) and Soya bean are pulses or legumes, known for their high protein content. Rice is a cereal, which is primarily a source of carbohydrates.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Discuss traditional versus modern culinary practices in India.
items.answer: Traditional Culinary Practices : These methods often emphasize using fresh, local, and seasonal ingredients. Cooking techniques might include slow cooking over fire, grinding spices by hand using a mortar and pestle, fermentation (like for idli or dosa), and using traditional cookware like earthen pots or iron kadhais. Meals are often balanced based on regional traditions or Ayurvedic principles. These methods can be time- consuming but often preserve nutrients well and use less processed ingredients. Modern Culinary Practices : These often prioritize speed and convenience. They involve using pressure cookers, microwave ovens, mixers/ grinders, and non-stick cookware. There’s a greater reliance on processed foods, packaged ingredients, ready-made spice mixes, and frozen items. Refrigeration is common for storage. Modern practices also show influences from global cuisines and include fast food and ready- to-eat meals. While convenient, these practices may involve higher consumption of preservatives, unhealthy fats, sugar, and salt, and potentially lower nutrient retention in some processed foods.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: A teacher says that good food may act as medicine. Ravi is curious about this statement and has some questions for his teacher. List at least two questions that he can ask.
items.answer: Ravi could ask questions like: How can eating specific foods help our body fight diseases or recover from illness? Can you give examples of foods that are known to have medicinal properties and what health benefits they provide?

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Not all delicious foods are necessarily healthy, while not all nutritious foods are always enjoyable. Share your thoughts along with a few examples.
items.answer: Thoughts : It’s true that taste and health don’t always go hand-in-hand. Many foods engineered to be delicious (like chips, sugary drinks, candies, pizza, fried snacks) are high in sugar, salt, unhealthy fats, and refined flour, offering minimal nutrition and potentially harming health if eaten often. Conversely, some highly nutritious foods (like bitter gourd/karela, spinach for some, plain oats) might not appeal to everyone’s taste initially. The goal should be balance : make healthy foods tastier (using spices, varied cooking methods) and enjoy less healthy ‘delicious’ foods in moderation as occasional treats. Learning to appreciate natural tastes of nutritious food is key for long-term health. Examples : Delicious but often unhealthy : French fries, sugary soda, candy, deep-fried samosas. Nutritious but sometimes less enjoyed : Bitter gourd (karela), plain boiled spinach, unsweetened oats porridge.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why might food choices and preparation practices differ from one another across different regions?

options.label: A
options.text: Due to a lack of cooking skills in certain areas

options.label: B
options.text: Because all regions have access to the same ingredients

options.label: C
options.text: Influenced by local crop cultivation, taste preferences, culture, and traditions

options.label: D
options.text: Solely because of government regulations on food

items.answer: (C) Influenced by local crop cultivation, taste preferences, culture, and traditions. Food habits are shaped by a combination of factors including what can be grown locally, cultural heritage, established traditions, and the collective taste preferences of a community.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are carbohydrates primarily known for in our diet?

options.label: C
options.text: Being a primary source of energy

options.label: D
options.text: Aiding in the digestion of food

items.answer: (C) Being a primary source of energy. Carbohydrates, such as those found in cereals, potatoes, and fruits, are a major food component that provides the body with the energy required for various activities and bodily functions.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which of the following food items is mentioned as a source of carbohydrates?
items.answer: (C) Potato Potatoes, various cereals including wheat and rice, plus fruits such as bananas, are typical food sources high in carbohydrates, which in turn give the body its energy.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why are carbohydrates and fats referred to as ‘energy-giving foods’? are essential for water absorption.

options.text: Because they help in repairing body tissues

options.label: B
options.text: Because they protect the body against infections

options.label: C
options.text: Because they provide the body with the necessary energy for activities

items.answer: (C) Because they provide the body with the necessary energy for activities. Both carbohydrates and fats are major sources of energy for the body. Carbohydrates provide immediate energy, while fats serve as a stored energy source, supporting various bodily functions and physical activities.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are proteins primarily known for in terms of their function in the body?

options.label: A
options.text: Providing instant energy for short bursts of activity

options.label: B
options.text: Protecting the body by forming a barrier against germs

options.label: C
options.text: Helping in the growth and repair of body tissues

items.answer: (C) Helping in the growth and repair of body tissues. Proteins are essential nutrients often referred to as body-building foods because they play a crucial role in the growth, maintenance, and repair of the body’s tissues and muscles.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body

items.answer: (C) Eggs Examples of animal-based protein sources include milk, paneer, eggs, fish, and meat, while plant- based sources include soya bean, moong dal, and peas.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: While using iodine in the laboratory, a few drops of iodine fell on Mishti’s socks and a few fell on her teacher’s saree. The drops of iodine on the saree turned blue-black while the colour on the socks did not change. What can be a possible reason?
items.answer: The likely reason is that the teacher’s saree contained starch (possibly from being starched after washing to make it stiff), which reacts with iodine to turn blue-black. Mishti’s socks were probably made from materials like cotton (cellulose), wool, or synthetic fibers (nylon, polyester) that do not contain starch, hence no color change occurred with iodine.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why are millets considered a healthy choice of food? Can eating just millets suffice for the nutritional requirements of the body? Discuss.
items.answer: Why millets are healthy : Millets are considered healthy because they are rich in dietary fiber, minerals (like iron, magnesium), protein (compared to refined grains), and antioxidants. Many are gluten-free and have a lower glycemic index. Sufficiency of eating only millets : No, eating only millets is not sufficient for all nutritional needs. Discussion : A balanced diet requires nutrients from diverse food groups. Relying solely on millets can lead to deficiencies in some essential amino acids, vitamins (like C, B12), and fatty acids. A healthy diet should combine millets with pulses, various vegetables, fruits, nuts/seeds, and possibly dairy or other protein sources to cover all nutritional requirements.

items.stem: You are provided the following: (i) Canned fruit juice (ii) Fresh fruit juice (iii) Fresh fruit Which one would you prefer and why?
items.answer: Preference : (iii) Fresh fruit. Why : Fresh fruit provides maximum dietary fiber, vitamins, and minerals in their natural form. Fiber aids digestion and helps manage blood sugar. Fresh fruit juice (ii) loses most fiber during juicing. Canned fruit juice (i) often has added sugars, preservatives, reduced vitamin content, and lacks fiber, making it the least healthy option. Eating the whole fresh fruit is the most beneficial.

items.stem: Gourav got a fracture in his leg. His doctor aligned the bones and put on a plaster. The doctor also gave him calcium tablets. items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Sugar is an example of carbohydrates. Sugar is tested with iodine solution but it does not change to blue-black colour. What can be a possible reason?
items.answer: The iodine test specifically detects the presence of starch, which is a complex carbohydrate. Common table sugar (sucrose) is a simple carbohydrate. Simple sugars like glucose, fructose, and sucrose do not react with iodine solution to give the characteristic blue-black color. Therefore, even though sugar is a carbohydrate, it doesn’t give a positive iodine test because it is not starch.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What do you think of Raman’s statement, All starches are carbohydrates but not all carbohydrates are starches. Describe the design of an activity to test your answer.
items.answer: Opinion on statement : Raman’s statement is correct. Starch is a type of carbohydrate, so all starches belong to the carbohydrate group. However, carbohydrates also include simple sugars (like table sugar) and other complex forms (like cellulose), which are not starch. Carbohydrates are mainly energy-giving foods, providing fuel for the body’s activities. Proteins, on the other hand, are body-building foods, essential for the growth and repair of tissues.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: A growing child needs an adequate amount of a specific nutrient for proper growth and development of muscles and tissues. Which nutrient is most critical for this purpose?
items.answer: (C) Proteins Proteins are known as body-building foods and are essential for the growth and repair of tissues. Therefore, they are particularly crucial in the diet of growing children for their proper physical development.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is scurvy?

options.label: A
options.text: A disease caused by a deficiency of Vitamin D

options.label: B
options.text: A condition characterized by poor vision in darkness

options.label: C
options.text: A disease with symptoms like bleeding and swollen gums, caused by Vitamin C deficiency

options.label: D
options.text: A disorder related to the thyroid gland due to lack of iodine

items.answer: (C) A disease with symptoms like bleeding and swollen gums, caused by Vitamin C deficiency. Scurvy is a deficiency disease primarily caused by a lack of Vitamin C. Its characteristic symptoms include bleeding gums, swollen gums, and slow healing of wounds.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which types of fruits were observed by James Lind to help sailors recover from scurvy?
items.answer: (C) Lemons and oranges James Lind observed that sailors who ate citrus fruits such as lemons and oranges recovered from scurvy, as these fruits are rich in Vitamin C.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why was iodized salt introduced to the population in the Himalayan region and Northern plains of India?

options.label: A
options.text: To improve the taste of common salt

options.label: B
options.text: To combat goitre caused by iodine deficiency in their local food and water

options.label: C
options.text: To provide an additional source of energy

options.label: D
options.text: To help in the digestion of food more effectively

items.answer: (B) To combat goitre caused by iodine deficiency in their local food and water. The prevalence of goitre (swelling at the front of the neck) was linked to iodine deficiency in the soil of these regions, leading to insufficient iodine in the diet. Iodized salt was introduced to supplement iodine intake.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are nutrients?

options.label: A
options.text: Substances in food that primarily add flavor and color

options.label: B
options.text: Components in food that provide energy, support growth, repair, and protect the body

options.label: C
options.text: Only the vitamins and minerals present in fruits and vegetables

options.label: D
options.text: The indigestible parts of food that aid in bowel movement

items.answer: (B) Components in food that provide energy, support growth, repair, and protect the body. Nutrients are essential substances found in food that the body needs for energy, growth, maintenance, repair of tissues, and protection against diseases. They include carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT considered a major nutrient for the human body?
items.answer: (C) Water Although water is vital for the body, the main nutrients listed are carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals. Water and dietary fiber are also recognized as essential components of a balanced diet.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which vitamin is naturally produced by our body upon exposure to sunlight?
items.answer: (D) Vitamin D Vitamin D is naturally produced in the body when the skin is exposed to sunlight, and it plays a key role in helping the body absorb calcium for strong and healthy bones.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why is it advisable to include uncooked vegetables and fruits in our diet?

options.label: A
options.text: Because cooking always enhances all nutrient content

options.label: B
options.text: Because some nutrients, like Vitamin C, can be lost during cooking due to heat

options.label: C
options.text: Because uncooked foods are always easier to digest for everyone

options.label: D
options.text: Because cooking removes all dietary fibres from food

items.answer: (B) Because some nutrients, like Vitamin C, can be lost during cooking due to heat. Cooking processes, especially those involving high heat, can lead to the loss of certain heat-sensitive vitamins, such as Vitamin C. Including some raw fruits and vegetables helps retain these nutrients.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is another term for dietary fibres?
items.answer: (D) Roughage Dietary fibres are also commonly known as roughage. While they do not provide nutrients, they are crucial for healthy digestion and bowel movements.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which of the following food groups is a good source of roughage?

options.label: C
options.text: Green leafy vegetables, fresh fruits, and whole grains

items.answer: (C) Green leafy vegetables, fresh fruits, and wholegrains Plant-based foods such as green leafy vegetables, fresh fruits, whole grains, pulses, and nuts are recognized as good sources of roughage or dietary fibre.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: An individual is experiencing frequent constipation. A doctor advises them to increase their intake of a particular food component that helps in smooth passage of stools. This advice emphasizes the importance of increasing:
items.answer: (C) Dietary fibres Dietary fibres (roughage) add bulk to the stool and aid in regular bowel movements, preventing constipation. Whole fruits and salads are rich sources of dietary fibres.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: How does water primarily help the body in relation to nutrients?

options.label: A
options.text: Water itself is a major source of energy

options.label: B
options.text: Water helps the body absorb nutrients from food

options.label: C
options.text: Water converts carbohydrates directly into proteins

options.label: D
options.text: Water significantly increases the fat content of food

items.answer: (B) Water helps the body absorb nutrients from food. Water plays a vital role in the digestive process by helping to dissolve nutrients from food, making them available for absorption and utilization by the body.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which scientist is credited with initiating nutrition research in India and analyzing Indian foods for their nutritional value?
items.answer: (C) Coluthur Gopalan Coluthur Gopalan is recognized as the scientist who pioneered nutrition research in India, studied the nutritional content of various Indian foods, and contributed to the development of programs such as the Mid Day Meal Scheme.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What color change indicates the presence of starch when diluted iodine solution is added to a food item?
items.answer: (C) The food item turns blue-black. The test for starch involves adding a few drops of diluted iodine solution to the food sample. A blue-black coloration indicates that starch is present in the food item.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: If you rub a piece of groundnut on paper and it leaves an oily patch that makes the paper translucent, what nutrient is present in the groundnut?
items.answer: (C) Fat The test for fats involves rubbing the food item on paper. If an oily patch appears, making the paper translucent (allowing light to pass through faintly), it indicates the presence of fat.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What chemicals are typically used to test for the presence of proteins in a food item, as described in Activity 3.7?

options.label: B
options.text: Copper sulphate solution and caustic soda solution

items.answer: (B) Copper sulphate solution and caustic soda solution. The test for proteins described involves adding copper sulphate solution and caustic soda solution to the food sample. A violet color indicates the presence of proteins.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is a balanced diet?

options.label: A
options.text: A diet consisting of only fruits and vegetables

options.label: B
options.text: A diet that includes all essential nutrients, roughage, and water in the right amounts

options.label: C
options.text: A diet rich in fats and carbohydrates for maximum energy

options.label: D
options.text: A diet that changes every day to include different food items

items.answer: (B) A diet that includes all essential nutrients, roughage, and water in the right amounts. A balanced diet is one that provides all the necessary nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals), along with adequate dietary fibre and water, in appropriate proportions to maintain good health.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why are junk foods generally considered unhealthy if consumed frequently?

options.label: B
options.text: They have high calories from sugar and fat but low amounts of essential nutrients

options.label: C
options.text: They take a very long time to cook

options.label: D
options.text: They are only made from plant sources

items.answer: (B) They have high calories from sugar and fat but low amounts of essential nutrients. Junk foods often provide a lot of calories, primarily from unhealthy fats and sugars, but lack significant amounts of proteins, vitamins, minerals, and dietary fibres, making them nutritionally poor.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which organization in India is responsible for regulating food quality?

options.label: B
options.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

options.label: C
options.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)

items.answer: (C) Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is the government body responsible for regulating and ensuring food quality and safety across the country.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are millets, such as jowar, bajra, and ragi, also called due to their high nutritional value?
items.answer: (C) Nutri-cereals Millets are referred to as nutri-cereals because they are highly nutritious, being good sources of vitamins, minerals (like iron and calcium), and dietary fibres.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What does the term ‘food miles’ refer to?

options.label: A
options.text: The average distance a person walks after eating food

options.label: B
options.text: The total distance a food item travels from the producer to the consumer

options.label: C
options.text: The number of miles a farmer travels to sell produce

options.label: D
options.text: The caloric energy obtained by traveling a mile

items.answer: (B) The total distance a food item travels from the producer to the consumer. Food miles represent the entire distance a food product covers from its point of origin (farm or production site) to the end consumer’s plate. Reducing food miles is environmentally beneficial.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Assertion (A) : Consuming a diet rich in fruits, vegetables, and whole grains is generally considered healthy. Reason (R) : These foods are good sources of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fibres.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Fruits, vegetables, and whole grains are indeed considered healthy because they provide essential vitamins, minerals, and dietary fibres, which contribute to overall well-being and proper bodily functions.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Carbohydrates are a primary source of energy. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
items.answer: (B) 3 only Proteins are body-building foods. Vitamins and minerals are needed in small quantities. Carbohydrates are a primary energy source. Thus, only statement 3 is correct.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: A person often feels tired, has bleeding gums, and their wounds heal very slowly. Their diet mainly consists of processed foods and lacks fresh fruits. This person is likely suffering from a deficiency of:
items.answer: (B) Vitamin C Bleeding gums and slow wound healing are classic symptoms of scurvy, which is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin C. Fresh fruits, especially citrus fruits, are rich sources of Vitamin C.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which traditional Indian cooking tool, made of stone, was earlier used for manual grinding?
items.answer: (B) Sil-batta The sil-batta, a traditional stone grinder, was commonly used to manually grind spices and other food ingredients before electric grinders became widely available.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is the main purpose of the PM POSHAN initiative (formerly Mid Day Meal Programme) in schools?

options.label: B
options.text: To provide balanced food to improve the health and nutrition of children

options.label: C
options.text: To reduce the burden of parents packing lunch

options.label: D
options.text: To promote local cuisines among students

items.answer: (B) To provide balanced food to improve the health and nutrition of children. The Mid Day Meal Programme, now PM POSHAN, was implemented to address nutritional deficiencies by providing balanced meals to children in government and government- aided schools, thereby improving their health and nutritional status.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is the term for the process of adding more nutrients to food during processing to improve its nutritional quality?
items.answer: (C) Fortification Fortification is the process of deliberately increasing the content of one or more essential micronutrients (vitamins or minerals) in a food to improve its nutritional quality and prevent deficiencies.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: How does the nutritional profile of roasted chana generally compare to potato wafers, based on the information in Activity 3.9?

options.label: A
options.text: Potato wafers have more protein and dietary fibre

options.label: B
options.text: Roasted chana has more protein and dietary fibre

options.label: C
options.text: Both have almost identical amounts of fats and carbohydrates

options.label: D
options.text: Potato wafers are lower in total energy (kcal)

items.answer: (B) Roasted chana has more protein and dietary fibre. Nutritional information showing that roasted chana typically has significantly more protein and dietary fibre, and less fat, compared to potato wafers, making it a healthier snack option.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a primary function of water in our diet?

options.label: A
options.text: Helping the body absorb nutrients from food

options.label: B
options.text: Removing waste from the body through sweat and urine

options.label: D
options.text: Maintaining overall health when consumed sufficiently

items.answer: (C) Providing significant amounts of energy. Water is essential for absorbing nutrients, eliminating waste, and overall health, but it does not provide caloric energy like carbohydrates, fats, or proteins do.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: A person is advised to spend some time in sunlight daily to help their body absorb calcium for better bone health. This advice is related to the body’s production of which vitamin?
items.answer: (D) Vitamin D Exposure to sunlight enables the body to produce Vitamin D. Vitamin D, in turn, plays a crucial role in the absorption of calcium, which is essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Assertion (A) : Goitre is caused by a deficiency of iodine. Reason (R) : Iodine is essential for the proper functioning of the thyroid gland.

options.label: A
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: B
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: C
options.text: A is true, but R is false

options.label: D
options.text: A is false, but R is true

items.answer: (A) Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Goitre, characterized by swelling in the neck, is a direct result of iodine deficiency. Iodine is a crucial component needed by the thyroid gland to produce hormones that regulate metabolism.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: A marathon runner is seen drinking glucose water during a race. Why is glucose water beneficial in this situation?

options.label: A
options.text: It helps in building muscle mass quickly

options.label: B
options.text: Glucose provides instant energy to the body

options.label: C
options.text: It primarily helps in repairing worn-out tissues

options.label: D
options.text: It is mainly for hydrating, with no energy benefit

items.answer: (B) Glucose provides instant energy to the body. Glucose is a simple carbohydrate that is readily absorbed by the body and converted into energy. This provides a quick fuel source for athletes during endurance activities like a marathon.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which of the following is mentioned as a symptom of Beriberi, a disease caused by Vitamin B1 deficiency?

options.label: A
options.text: Bleeding gums and slow healing of wounds

options.label: C
options.text: Swelling, tingling, or burning sensation in feet and hands

items.answer: (C) Swelling, tingling, or burning sensation in feet and hands. Beriberi, resulting from Vitamin B1 deficiency, can manifest with symptoms such as swelling, tingling or burning sensation in feet and hands, and trouble in breathing.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is the significance of food miles in the context of environmental health and supporting local economies?

options.label: A
options.text: Higher food miles are always better for food freshness

options.label: B
options.text: Reducing food miles can cut down transport pollution and support local farmers

options.label: C
options.text: Food miles only refer to the distance food travels within a single city

options.label: D
options.text: The concept of food miles is irrelevant to environmental concerns

items.answer: (B) Reducing food miles can cut down transport pollution and support local farmers. Shorter food miles mean less transportation, which reduces fuel consumption and pollution. It also often means supporting local agricultural producers and potentially getting fresher produce.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are protective nutrients?

options.label: A
options.text: Nutrients that provide the most calories for energy

options.label: B
options.text: Nutrients like proteins that help build body tissues

options.label: C
options.text: Vitamins and minerals that protect the body from diseases and keep it healthy

options.label: D
options.text: Dietary fibres that aid in digestion

items.answer: (C) Vitamins and minerals that protect the body from diseases and keep it healthy. Vitamins and minerals are often referred to as protective nutrients because they play vital roles in maintaining the immune system, protecting against various diseases, and ensuring overall health.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a good source of fat?
items.answer: (B) Rice Various sources of fats including nuts, seeds, oils and butter. Rice is primarily a source of carbohydrates, not fats.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is a key difference in the energy provision by carbohydrates versus fats?

options.label: A
options.text: Carbohydrates provide stored energy; fats provide instant energy

options.label: B
options.text: Fats provide instant energy; carbohydrates provide stored energy

options.label: C
options.text: Carbohydrates are primary for instant energy; fats are a source of stored energy

options.label: D
options.text: Neither carbohydrates nor fats provide significant energy

items.answer: (C) Carbohydrates are primary for instant energy; fats are a source of stored energy. Carbohydrates are the body’s preferred source for quick, readily available energy. Fats, being more energy-dense, serve as a reserve or stored form of energy.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: All of these are symptoms of Vitamin A deficiency EXCEPT:

options.label: B
options.text: Loss of vision in darkness (night blindness)

options.label: C
options.text: Swelling at the front of the neck

items.answer: (C) Swelling at the front of the neck. Poor vision, night blindness, and potential complete loss of vision are symptoms associated with Vitamin A deficiency. Swelling at the front of the neck is a symptom of goitre, caused by iodine deficiency.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: To prevent rickets, which is characterized by soft and bent bones, a diet should include adequate amounts of:
items.answer: (B) Vitamin D and Calcium. Rickets is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin D, which is necessary for calcium absorption. Calcium is crucial for bone health. Therefore, both Vitamin D and Calcium are vital in preventing rickets.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is the meaning of the Sanskrit saying ‘annena jatani jivanti’?
items.answer: Food gives life to living beings.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: On what factor is the traditional food of any state usually based?
items.answer: The traditional food of any state is usually based on the crops grown in that state.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Name one traditional cooking tool and one modern cooking tool.
items.answer: Traditional : chulha ; Modern : gas stove.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is the primary function of carbohydrates in our diet?
items.answer: Carbohydrates are one of the primary sources of energy in our diet.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Give one example of a food item rich in fats.
items.answer: Ghee (or nuts, oils, etc.).

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why are carbohydrates and fats called energy- giving foods?
items.answer: They provide us energy for performing various activities.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is the main role of proteins in the body?
items.answer: Proteins help in the growth and repair of our body.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Name one plant source of protein.
items.answer: Pulses (or beans, peas, nuts).

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What disease is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin C?
items.answer: Scurvy is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin C.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is the main symptom of goitre?
items.answer: Swelling at the front of the neck is a symptom of goitre.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Which mineral deficiency causes goitre?
items.answer: Goitre is caused by a deficiency of iodine.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Name one food source of Vitamin A.
items.answer: Papaya (or carrot, mango, milk).

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is the function of Vitamin D in our body?
items.answer: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium for bone and teeth health.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is another name for dietary fibres?
items.answer: Dietary fibres are also known as roughage.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What colour change indicates the presence of starch in a food item when tested with iodine solution?
items.answer: A blue-black colour indicates the presence of starch.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is a balanced diet?
items.answer: A diet that has all essential nutrients, roughage, and water in the right amount for proper growth and development of the body.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are millets also called due to their high nutritional value?
items.answer: Millets are also called nutri-cereals.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What does FSSAI stand for?
items.answer: Food Safety and Standard Authority of India.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why is there diversity in the food consumed in different regions of India?
items.answer: Food diversity in India is due to varied soil types and climatic conditions influencing crop cultivation, alongside regional taste preferences, culture, and traditions.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: How have cooking practices changed over time? Give two examples.
items.answer: Cooking practices have shifted from traditional to modern methods. For example, chulhas have been replaced by gas stoves, and manual grinding with sil-battas has given way to electrical grinders.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why does a marathon runner drink glucose water during a race?
items.answer: A marathon runner drinks glucose water because glucose, a carbohydrate, provides instant energy, which is crucial for sustaining performance during a long race.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are fats? Name two plant sources and two animal sources of fats.
items.answer: Fats are energy-giving food components that serve as stored energy. Plant sources include nuts (e.g., almonds) and seeds (e.g., sunflower seeds); animal sources include ghee and butter.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why are proteins called body-building foods? Who needs proteins in larger quantities?
items.answer: Proteins are called body-building foods because they help in the growth and repair of our body. Sportspersons need proteins in larger quantities to build their muscles.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are vitamins and minerals also called? Why are they essential for our body?
items.answer: Vitamins and minerals are also called protective nutrients. They are essential because they protect our body from diseases and keep us healthy, required in small amounts.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What did James Lind observe about sailors during his voyage in 1746? What conclusion was drawn?
items.answer: James Lind observed that sailors who consumed lemons and oranges recovered from bleeding and swollen gums. The conclusion was that citrus fruits cure scurvy, caused by Vitamin C deficiency.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What problem was observed in the Himalayan region regarding health in the 1960s? How was it addressed?
items.answer: Symptoms of swelling at the front of the neck (goitre) were prevalent due to iodine deficiency. This was addressed by supplementing common salt with iodine to make iodised salt.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: List two functions and two sources of Vitamin B.
items.answer: Vitamin B keeps the heart healthy and supports the body in performing various functions. Sources include legumes, nuts, whole grains, seeds and milk products.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are the symptoms of anaemia? Which mineral deficiency causes it and what are its food sources?
items.answer: Symptoms of anaemia include weakness and shortness of breath. It is caused by iron deficiency. Food sources include green leafy vegetables, beetroot, and pomegranate.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why is it important to include fruits and uncooked vegetables in our diet?
items.answer: Including fruits and uncooked vegetables is important because some nutrients, like Vitamin C, can be lost during cooking due to high heat.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What is roughage and why is it an essential component of our food despite not providing nutrients?
items.answer: Roughage, or dietary fibre, is mainly plant products that do not provide nutrients but are essential for helping our body get rid of undigested food and ensuring smooth passage of stools.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: How does water help our body? Why should we drink sufficient water?
items.answer: Water helps the body absorb nutrients from food and removes waste through sweat and urine. We should drink sufficient water to keep ourselves healthy.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are the three main nutrients that can be detected by simple tests?
items.answer: Starch (a type of carbohydrate), fat, and protein can be detected using fairly simple tests in a school laboratory setting.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: How can you test for the presence of fats in a food item?
items.answer: Place a small amount of the food item on paper, wrap and press it. An oily patch on the paper, which makes it translucent, indicates the presence of fat.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Describe the test for proteins in a food item. What indicates a positive result?
items.answer: Make a paste of the food, add water, then two drops of copper sulphate solution and ten drops of caustic soda solution. A violet colour indicates the presence of proteins.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why might nutritional requirements vary from person to person?
items.answer: Nutritional requirements vary based on age, gender, physical activity levels, health status, and lifestyle. Different individuals need different types and amounts of nutrients.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are junk foods? Why is frequent consumption of junk food not good for health?
items.answer: Junk foods are high in calories, sugar, and fat, but low in proteins, minerals, vitamins, and dietary fibres. Frequent consumption can lead to obesity and other health problems.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are millets and why are they considered highly nutritious?
items.answer: Millets are small-sized grains like jowar and bajra. They are highly nutritious as they are good sources of vitamins, minerals (like iron and calcium), and dietary fibres.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Why is reducing food miles important? Give two reasons.
items.answer: Reducing food miles is important as it helps cut down transport costs and pollution, supports local farmers, and keeps food fresh and healthy.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Explain the relationship between locally grown crops and the traditional food items of a region. Why does this diversity exist across India?
items.answer: The traditional food of a region is usually based on the crops that are locally grown there, which in turn depend on the soil type and climatic conditions. India, being an agricultural country with diverse geography, supports various crops in different regions, leading to a rich diversity in food habits influenced also by culture and taste.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are the major nutrients found in our food? Briefly describe the main function of carbohydrates, fats, and proteins. Give two food sources for each.
items.answer: Major nutrients are carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, and minerals. Carbohydrates (e.g., rice, potato) and fats (e.g., oil, nuts) are primary energy sources. Proteins (e.g., pulses, milk) are body-building foods, essential for growth and repair of the body.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are deficiency diseases? Explain with the examples of scurvy and rickets, including their causes, symptoms, and food sources that can help.
items.answer: Deficiency diseases occur due to the lack of one or more essential nutrients in the diet over a long period. Scurvy, caused by Vitamin C deficiency (sources: citrus fruits), leads to bleeding gums and slow wound healing. Rickets, from Vitamin D deficiency (sources: sunlight, milk, eggs), causes soft and bent bones.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Describe the role of vitamins A, B, C, and D in maintaining health. For each vitamin, list one key function and one common food source.
items.answer: Vitamin A keeps eyes and skin healthy (source: carrot). Vitamin B keeps the heart healthy and supports body functions (source: whole grains). Vitamin C helps the body fight diseases (source: lemon). Vitamin D helps absorb calcium for bones (source: sunlight, milk).

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are dietary fibres and water? Explain why they are considered essential components of a balanced diet even though dietary fibres do not provide nutrients.
items.answer: Dietary fibres (roughage) are plant-based components that aid in digestion and bowel movement. Water is vital for absorbing nutrients and removing waste. Though fibres don’t provide nutrients, they ensure smooth digestion and prevent constipation, making them crucial for a balanced diet.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Explain the process for testing the presence of starch and protein in given food samples. What observations would indicate a positive result for each test?
items.answer: For starch, add 2-3 drops of dilute iodine solution to the food sample; a blue-black colour indicates starch. For protein, make a paste of the food, add water, 2 drops of copper sulphate, and 10 drops of caustic soda solution; a violet colour indicates protein.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What constitutes a balanced diet? Why is it important to consume a balanced diet? What changes might you suggest to a person whose diet is not balanced?
items.answer: A balanced diet contains all essential nutrients, roughage, and water in the right proportions for proper growth and development. It is important for maintaining good health and preventing diseases. One should include a variety of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, pulses, and dairy, and reduce junk food.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: What are millets? Why are they gaining popularity and referred to as ‘nutri-cereals’? Mention any two benefits of including millets in our diet.
items.answer: Millets are small-sized grains like jowar, bajra, and ragi. They are gaining popularity due to their numerous health benefits and are called ‘nutri- cereals’ because they are rich sources of vitamins, minerals (iron, calcium), and dietary fibres. Benefits include contributing to a balanced diet and being easily cultivable.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Explain the concept of ‘food miles’. How does eating locally grown food help in reducing food miles and what are the broader benefits of this practice?
items.answer: Food miles refer to the distance food travels from the farm to the consumer. Eating locally grown food reduces this distance, thereby lowering transportation costs and pollution. It also supports local farmers, ensures fresher food, and benefits the environment.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Health is the Ultimate Wealth. Explain this statement in the context of eating habits. How can mindful eating contribute to good health? (Evaluating)
items.answer: This statement means good health is more valuable than any material wealth. Poor eating habits, like consuming excessive junk food, can lead to diseases, diminishing quality of life. Mindful eating, which involves choosing a balanced diet and avoiding unhealthy foods, directly contributes to maintaining good health.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Rohan is a 12-year-old boy who loves eating packaged chips and sugary drinks every day after school. He often complains of feeling tired and finds it difficult to concentrate on his studies. His mother notices he rarely eats fruits or vegetables. (i) What types of food components are likely high in Rohan’s current snack choices? (ii) Which essential nutrients might be lacking in Rohan’s diet based on his food preferences? (iii) What health problems might Rohan face in the long run if he continues with these eating habits? (iv) Suggest two simple dietary changes Rohan can make to improve his health.
items.answer: (i) Rohan’s snacks (packaged chips and sugary drinks) are likely high in fats, sugar (a carbohydrate), and calories. (ii) Rohan’s diet might be lacking in vitamins, minerals, proteins, and dietary fibres as he rarely eats fruits or vegetables. (iii) Rohan might face health problems like obesity, dental issues, nutritional deficiencies, and reduced energy levels, impacting his growth and concentration. (iv) Rohan can replace packaged chips with roasted chana or fruits, and sugary drinks with water, milk, or fresh fruit juice.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: A remote village community primarily consumes polished rice and a limited variety of locally grown vegetables. Many children in the community show symptoms like poor vision, especially in dim light, and often fall sick. (i) Which vitamin deficiency is likely causing poor vision in dim light among the children? (ii) What types of food should be included in their diet to address this deficiency? (iii) Why might consuming only polished rice contribute to nutritional deficiencies?
items.answer: (i) The poor vision in dim light (night blindness) is likely caused by a deficiency of Vitamin A. (ii) Foods rich in Vitamin A like papaya, carrots, mangoes, milk, and green leafy vegetables should be included in their diet. (iii) Polishing rice removes the outer layers which contain essential nutrients like Vitamin B1and dietary fibre, leading to potential deficiencies.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: During a science class, students performed tests on different food items. When iodine solution was added to a boiled potato slice, it turned blue- black. When a few drops of oil were pressed on paper, it left an oily, translucent patch. (i) What nutrient is confirmed to be present in the boiled potato slice? (ii) What nutrient is indicated by the oily, translucent patch left by the oil? (iii) If a food item like groundnuts showed positive results for both the paper test (oily patch) and the violet colour test with copper sulphate and caustic soda, what nutrients does it contain?
items.answer: (i) Starch (a type of carbohydrate) is confirmed to be present in the boiled potato slice. (ii) Fat is indicated by the oily, translucent patch. (iii) Groundnuts would contain both fats and proteins.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: Mrs. Sharma wants to ensure her family eats healthy. She read that including millets is beneficial. She decides to replace some of their regular wheat chapati meals with ragi (finger millet) dosas and bajra (pearl millet) khichdi. (i) What are two nutritional benefits Mrs. Sharma’s family will get from including ragi and bajra? (ii) Besides nutritional benefits, how might choosing millets also be environmentally beneficial? (iii) What does the term ‘nutri-cereals’ signify about millets?
items.answer: (i) Her family will get good amounts of dietary fibre, minerals like iron and calcium, and various vitamins from ragi and bajra. (ii) Millets can be easily cultivated in different climatic conditions and often require less water than wheat or rice, making them environmentally beneficial. (iii)‘Nutri-cereals’ signifies that millets are highly nutritious grains, providing many essential components required for the normal functioning of our body.

items.chapter: Mindful Eating : A Path to a Healthy Body
items.stem: An elderly person, Mr. Gupta, has been advised by his doctor to increase his fibre intake due to persistent constipation. He usually eats white bread sandwiches for breakfast and avoids salads, thinking they are difficult to digest. (i) What is the role of dietary fibre in preventing constipation? (ii) Suggest two fibre-rich food items that Mr. Gupta can easily incorporate into his breakfast instead of white bread. (iii) Besides salads, what are two other good sources of dietary fibre Mr. Gupta could include in his other meals?
items.answer: (i) Dietary fibre (roughage) helps the body get rid of undigested food and ensures smooth passage of stools, thus preventing constipation. (ii) Mr. Gupta can incorporate whole-grain bread or oats (dalia/porridge) for breakfast to increase his fibre intake. (iii) Mr. Gupta could include whole fruits, pulses (like lentils and beans), and other vegetables (cooked or raw) in his other meals.
